correctness.rationale: At alpha=1 the four quarter-branches of each map send uniform measure bijectively onto a half-interval. This preserves conditional uniformity given any sequence of branches, and yields the marked transition weights. From the left half the nonzero weights to left and right are 1/2 and p/2, and the zero weight q/2 stays left; the right row is the reflected version with p and q swapped. The stationary row (q,p) and the stated eigenvalues follow. With B=diag(q/2,p/2) and P=M_p(1), the joint moment at lag k inserts B P^(k−1) B. The nonstationary projection contributes the factor 2^(−(k−1)) times the stationary variance of the two entries of B, namely h(1−4h)/4. At p=1/2 the next-zero conditional probability is 1/4 for any hidden-half distribution, giving IID digits; at any other interior p the lag-one covariance is positive. Summing covariances gives the finite variance, including N=1, and optimizing its asymptotic coefficient over 0<h≤1/4 gives the asserted minimum and maxima. The positive tilted matrix has an isolated simple Perron eigenvalue: the spectral prefactor tends to one in the centered t/sqrt(N) expansion, giving the CLT with variance Gamma. The limiting log-mgf is differentiable on the full real line and the normalized counts have compact support, yielding the full LDP. The eigenvalue limits at z→0 and after division by z at z→∞ give the two finite endpoint rates; equivalently the all-nonzero and all-zero events use M_p(0) and B respectively. These conclusions are annealed and stationary, not claims for a quenched or nonstationary law. The frozen finite verification was read as evidence, not executed or used to prove the limit statements.

value.rationale: The endpoint of the published signed-expansion model is a natural tractable case. The exact two-state law determines finite-sample zero-digit counts, and exposes a difference between mean-frequency analysis and variability: the fair switch has IID digits and minimizes asymptotic variance, while two biased switches maximize it. The explicit rare-event rates and the variance extrema are concrete information about the expansion statistics, not merely a general CLT citation.
